summary: The Sages said four kinds of nedarim do not count. The first kind is a neder said only to push someone, like when a buyer and seller bargain about a price.

chunks.en: The Sages said four kinds of nedarim do not count:
chunks.st: The Sages dissolved four types of vows

chunks.en: nedarim to push someone,
chunks.st: without the requirement of a request to a halakhic authority: Vows of exhortation,

chunks.en: and nedarim of exaggeration,
chunks.st: vows of exaggeration,

chunks.en: and nedarim by mistake,
chunks.st: vows that are unintentional,

chunks.en: and nedarim that a person could not keep because something stopped him.
chunks.st: and vows whose fulfillment is impeded by circumstances beyond one’s control.

chunks.en: What are nedarim to push someone?
chunks.st: The mishna explains: Vows of exhortation

chunks.en: How? Someone was selling something and said,
chunks.st: are those by which one encourages another using vow terminology that is exaggerated. How so? One was selling an item and said:

chunks.he: קוֹנָם שֶׁאֵינִי פוֹחֵת לְךָ מִן הַסֶּלַע,
chunks.en: "Konam, I will not take less than a sela from you!"
chunks.st: I will not lower the price for you to less than a sela, as that is konam, forbidden as if it were an offering, for me.

words.note: A silver coin, worth four dinars.

chunks.en: And the buyer says,
chunks.st: And the other one, the buyer, says:

chunks.he: קוֹנָם שֶׁאֵינִי מוֹסִיף לְךָ עַל הַשֶּׁקֶל,
chunks.en: "Konam, I will not give you more than a shekel!"
chunks.st: I will not raise my payment to you to more than a shekel, as that is konam for me.

chunks.en: Really, both of them want three dinars.
chunks.st: In this case, one may assume that both want to complete the deal at three dinars,

chunks.en: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says,
chunks.st: and they did not intend to vow but only exaggerated for purposes of bargaining. Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya’akov says:

chunks.en: Even someone who wants to make a neder for
chunks.st: Even one who wants to take a vow

chunks.en: his friend that he must eat with him
chunks.st: prohibiting another from benefiting from him, but only in order that he should eat with him,

chunks.en: should say, "Every neder that I will make
chunks.st: not intending to take an actual vow, should say to him at the outset: Any vow that I take in the future

chunks.en: does not count,"
chunks.st: is void.

chunks.en: as long as he remembers this when he makes the neder.
chunks.st: And this statement is effective, provided that he remembers at the time of the vow that his intent at the beginning of the year was to render it void.

summary: Here are examples of nedarim of exaggeration and nedarim by mistake. If a person made a neder because he thought something happened, and it did not happen, the neder does not count.

chunks.en: Nedarim of exaggeration:
chunks.st: Vows of exaggeration
chunks.stMore: that the Sages dissolved without a request to a halakhic authority, as described in the first mishna in the chapter, include the following examples.

chunks.en: he said, "Konam if I did not see
chunks.st: If one said concerning a certain item: It is konam for me if I did not see

chunks.en: on this road as many people as left Mitzrayim,"
chunks.st: on this road as many people as those who ascended from Egypt,

chunks.en: "if I did not see a snake
chunks.st: or if he said: It is konam for me if I did not see a snake

chunks.en: as big as the beam of an olive press."
chunks.st: as large as the beam of an olive press,
chunks.stMore: in these cases the speaker did not intend to vow but used hyperbole to demonstrate a point, and it is understood by others that the expression is not to be taken literally.

chunks.en: Nedarim by mistake:
chunks.st: What are examples of vows that are unintentional
chunks.stMore: that are dissolved, as taught at the beginning of the chapter? One who vows:

chunks.en: "if I ate," or "if I drank,"
chunks.st: This loaf is forbidden to me as if it were an offering [konam] if I ate or if I drank, and

chunks.en: and then he remembered that he did eat and drink.
chunks.st: then he remembers that he ate or drank.

chunks.en: "that I will eat," or "that I will drink,"
chunks.st: Or, one who vows: This loaf is konam for me if I will eat or if I will drink, and

chunks.en: and he forgot and ate and drank.
chunks.st: he then forgets and eats or drinks.

chunks.en: He said, "Konam, my wife may not benefit from me,
chunks.st: Also, one who said: Benefiting from me is konam for my wife

chunks.he: שֶׁגָּנְבָה אֶת כִּיסִי וְשֶׁהִכְּתָה אֶת בְּנִי,
chunks.en: because she stole my wallet, and because she hit my son,"
chunks.st: because she stole my purse or she hit my son, and

chunks.he: וְנוֹדַע שֶׁלֹּא הִכַּתּוּ וְנוֹדַע שֶׁלֹּא גְנָבָתּוּ.
chunks.en: and then it became known that she did not hit him and did not steal it.
chunks.st: then it became known that she had not hit him or it became known that she had not stolen.

chunks.en: He saw people eating his figs and said,
chunks.st: The mishna lists another example of an unintentional vow: One who saw people entering his courtyard and eating figs, and

chunks.en: "These are a korban for you!"
chunks.st: because he did not want them to do so he said: The figs are forbidden to you like an offering.

chunks.en: And it turned out they were his father and brothers,
chunks.st: And then it was found that his father and brother

words.en: and they turned out to be

chunks.en: and there were other people with them.
chunks.st: were in the group, and there were others with them
chunks.stMore: as well, and certainly he did not intend to take a vow prohibiting his father and brother from eating the figs.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: In such a case, Beit Shammai says:

chunks.en: they are permitted, and those with them are forbidden.
chunks.st: They, his father and brother, are permitted to eat the figs, and those others that were with them are prohibited

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: from doing so. And Beit Hillel says:

chunks.en: both groups are permitted.
chunks.st: Both these and those are permitted to eat the figs, as will be clarified in the Gemara.

summary: The fourth kind is a neder a person could not keep because something stopped him, like being sick or a river that he could not cross.

chunks.en: Nedarim that a person could not keep:
chunks.st: What are examples of vows impeded by circumstances beyond one’s control?

chunks.en: His friend made a neder that he must eat at his house,
chunks.st: If one’s friend took a vow with regard to him that he should eat with him, and

chunks.en: and he became sick, or
chunks.st: he became sick, or

chunks.en: his son became sick, or a river held him back,
chunks.st: his son became sick, or a river that he was unable to cross barred him

chunks.en: these are nedarim he could not keep.
chunks.st: from coming, these are examples of vows whose fulfillment are impeded by circumstances beyond one’s control. They are not binding and do not require dissolution.

summary: To protect himself from robbers or unfair tax collectors, a person may make a neder that is not true. Beis Shammai and Beis Hillel argue about how far he may go.

chunks.he: נוֹדְרִין לָהֳרָגִין וְלָחֳרָמִין וְלַמּוֹכְסִין שֶׁהִיא תְרוּמָה
chunks.en: One may make a neder to murderers, to robbers, and to tax collectors that it is terumah,
chunks.explain: This way they will not take his food.
chunks.st: One may take a vow to murderers, i.e., people suspected of killing others over monetary matters; or to robbers [ḥaramin]; or to tax collectors who wish to collect tax, that the produce in his possession is teruma

chunks.en: even though it is not terumah,
chunks.st: although it is not teruma.

chunks.en: or that it belongs to the king's house,
chunks.st: One may also take a vow to them that the produce in his possession belongs to the house of the king,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵינָן שֶׁל בֵּית הַמֶּלֶךְ.
chunks.en: even though it does not belong to the king's house.
chunks.st: although it does not belong to the house of the king.
chunks.stMore: One may take a false vow to save himself or his possessions, as a statement of this sort does not have the status of a vow.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he may make a neder with anything,
chunks.st: One may vow in such a case, although he has no intention that his words be true, using every

chunks.en: except with a shevuah.
chunks.st: means of taking a vow or making a prohibition in order to mislead those people, except for by taking of an oath,

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: due to its more stringent nature. And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even with a shevuah.
chunks.st: One may mislead them even by taking an oath.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: he should not be the first to offer a neder.
chunks.st: When negotiating with a robber, one should not initiate by taking a vow for him

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: unless the robber does not believe his claim, in which case he may take a vow to reinforce his words. And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: he may even be the first.
chunks.st: He may even initiate by taking a vow to him.

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: only what the robber makes him say.
chunks.st: One may take a vow only about that which the robber compels him to take a vow

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: but may not add to it. And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: even what the robber does not make him say.
chunks.st: One may take a vow even about that which he does not compel him to take a vow.

chunks.en: How? They told him,
chunks.st: The mishna explains the previous statement: How so? If the extortionist said to him

chunks.en: "Say: Konam, my wife may not benefit from me,"
chunks.st: that he should say: Benefiting from me is konam for my wife

chunks.he: וְאָמַר קוֹנָם אִשְׁתִּי וּבָנַי נֶהֱנִין לִי,
chunks.en: and he said, "Konam, my wife and my children may not benefit from me."
chunks.st: if the vow is not true, and he said: Benefiting from me is konam for my wife and my children,

chunks.en: Beis Shammai say,
chunks.st: Beit Shammai say:

chunks.en: his wife is permitted, and his children are forbidden.
chunks.st: His wife is permitted to benefit from him, since the extortionist demanded that he take that vow, but his children, whom he added of his own accord, are prohibited

chunks.en: But Beis Hillel say,
chunks.st: from benefiting from their father. And Beit Hillel say:

chunks.en: both are permitted.
chunks.st: Both these and those are permitted to benefit from him.

summary: When a person says his trees or his tallis are a korban, the exact words he uses decide whether they can be redeemed.

chunks.en: "These young trees are a korban
chunks.st: If one sees his property in danger of being destroyed, and takes a vow stating, for example: These saplings are like an offering

chunks.en: if they are not cut down,"
chunks.st: if they are not cut down,

chunks.he: טַלִּית זוֹ קָרְבָּן אִם אֵינָהּ נִשְׂרֶפֶת,
chunks.en: "This tallis is a korban if it is not burned,"
chunks.st: or: This garment is like an offering if it is not burned,

chunks.en: they can be redeemed.
chunks.st: these items are consecrated if the saplings remain standing or if the garment is not burned. In addition, they are subject to the possibility of redemption

chunks.he: הֲרֵי נְטִיעוֹת הָאֵלּוּ קָרְבָּן עַד שֶׁיִּקָּצְצוּ,
chunks.en: "These young trees are a korban until they are cut down,"
chunks.st: just as other items consecrated for maintenance of the Temple may be redeemed. But if one said: These saplings are like an offering until they are cut down,

chunks.en: "This tallis is a korban until it is burned,"
chunks.st: or: This garment is like an offering until it is burned,

chunks.en: they cannot be redeemed.
chunks.st: then they are not subject to the possibility of redemption.

summary: A neder about "people who go to sea" or "people who live on land" is understood the way people usually talk.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder not to benefit from people who go down to the sea
chunks.st: In the case of one who takes a vow that he will not derive benefit from seafarers,

words.en: from those who go down to

chunks.en: may benefit from people who live on land.
chunks.st: he is permitted to benefit from those who live on dry land.

chunks.en: If his neder was from people who live on land,
chunks.st: But if he takes a vow not to derive benefit from those who live on dry land,

chunks.en: he may not benefit from people who go to sea,
chunks.st: he is also prohibited from deriving benefit from seafarers,

words.en: with those who go down to

chunks.en: because people who go to sea are part of the people who live on land.
chunks.st: because seafarers are included within the category of those who live on dry land.

words.en: because those who go down to

chunks.en: Not people who just sail from Akko to Yafo,
chunks.st: The mishna now defines seafarers: Not like those that travel by ship from Akko to Jaffa,

chunks.en: but people who usually sail far away.
chunks.explain: They are the ones called "people who go to sea."
chunks.st: which is a short trip, but rather one who customarily departs [lefaresh] to distant locations, e.g., foreign countries.

summary: A neder not to benefit from "those who see the sun" includes even blind people, because he meant everyone the sun shines on.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder not to benefit from people who see the sun
chunks.st: One who takes a vow not to derive benefit from those who see the sun

chunks.en: may not benefit even from blind people,
chunks.st: is prohibited from deriving benefit even from the blind,

chunks.en: because he only meant
chunks.st: although they see nothing. This is because he meant only

chunks.en: people that the sun sees.
chunks.st: to include all those that the sun sees, i.e., shines upon with light.

summary: A neder not to benefit from "black-haired people" means grown men, even if they are bald or gray.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder not to benefit from people with black hair
chunks.st: One who takes a vow not to derive benefit from those that have dark heads [sheḥorei harosh]

chunks.en: may not benefit from bald people or gray-haired people,
chunks.st: is prohibited from deriving benefit from those that are bald, although they have no hair at all, and from the elderly
chunks.stMore: who have white hair. This is because the term is not to be understood in its simple meaning but rather in a broader manner.

chunks.en: but may benefit from women and children,
chunks.st: But he is permitted to derive benefit from women and from children,

chunks.he: שֶׁאֵין נִקְרָאִין שְׁחוֹרֵי הָרֹאשׁ אֶלָּא אֲנָשִׁים:
chunks.en: because only men are called "black-haired."
chunks.st: because only men are called: Those with dark heads.

summary: The mishnah explains what someone meant by a neder not to benefit from "those who are born." Rabbi Meir and the Sages argue.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder not to benefit from "yeludim"
chunks.st: One who takes a vow not to derive benefit from those that are born [yeludim]

chunks.en: may benefit from "noladim."
chunks.st: is permitted to derive benefit from those who will be born [noladim]

words.en: with the ones who will be born.

chunks.en: From "noladim,"
chunks.st: after the time of the vow. But if one takes a vow not to derive benefit from those who will be born,

words.en: the ones who will be born

chunks.en: he may not benefit from "yeludim."
chunks.st: he is also prohibited from deriving benefit from those that are already born at the time of the vow.

words.en: with the ones who are born.

chunks.en: Rabbi Meir permits even "yeludim."
chunks.st: Rabbi Meir permits deriving benefit even from those that are already born at the time of the vow

words.en: with the ones who are born.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: because he holds that the one taking the vow was precise in prohibiting only those that will be born. And the Rabbis say:

chunks.en: he only meant
chunks.st: He intended to include with this expression only

chunks.en: anyone who is born.
chunks.st: one whose nature is to be born. Therefore, both those who will be born and those who were already born are included in the vow.

summary: A neder not to benefit from "people who keep Shabbos" includes Kusim, but a neder about "people who go up to Yerushalayim" does not.

chunks.en: Someone who makes a neder not to benefit from people who keep Shabbos
chunks.st: One who takes a vow that deriving benefit from those who rest on Shabbat

chunks.en: may not benefit from Jews, and may not benefit from Kusim.
chunks.st: is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from a Jew, and he is also prohibited from deriving benefit from Samaritans [Kutim]

words.note: People who lived in Eretz Yisrael and kept some mitzvos.

chunks.en: From people who eat garlic,
chunks.st: because they are also Shabbat observers. One who takes a vow that deriving benefit from those who eat garlic

chunks.en: he may not benefit from Jews, and may not benefit from Kusim.
chunks.st: on Shabbat night is forbidden to him is prohibited from deriving benefit from a Jew, and he is also prohibited from benefiting from Samaritans.

chunks.en: From people who go up to Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: However, if one takes a vow that deriving benefit from those who ascend to Jerusalem

chunks.st: is forbidden to him, he is prohibited from deriving benefit from a Jew, but he is permitted to benefit from Samaritans because they do not ascend to Jerusalem, but rather, to Mount Gerizim.

summary: The mishnah explains nedarim about "children of Noach," "children of Avraham," and people with or without a bris milah. Then it praises how great the mitzvah of milah is.

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not benefit from the children of Noach,"
chunks.st: If one says: The property of the descendants of Noah is konam for me, and for that reason I will not benefit

chunks.en: he may benefit from Jews, but not from the other nations.
chunks.st: from it, he is permitted to derive benefit from a Jew but prohibited from deriving benefit from the nations of the world.

chunks.en: "that I will not benefit from the children of Avraham,"
chunks.st: If one says: The property of the offspring of Abraham is forbidden to me, and for that reason I will not benefit

chunks.en: he may not benefit from Jews, but may benefit from the other nations.
chunks.st: from it, he is prohibited from deriving benefit from a Jew but permitted to derive benefit from the nations of the world.

chunks.en: "that I will not benefit from Jews,"
chunks.st: If one says: The property of a Jew is forbidden to me, and for that reason I will not benefit

chunks.st: The property of a Jew is forbidden to me, and for that reason I will not benefit from them, and my property is forbidden to a Jew and they will not benefit from me,

chunks.st: in this case he may benefit from the nations of the world

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not benefit from people without a bris milah,"
chunks.st: but not from a Jew, and a Jew may not benefit from him. If one says: Benefiting from those who are uncircumcised is konam for me,

chunks.he: מֻתָּר בְּעַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאָסוּר בְּמוּלֵי הַגּוֹיִם.
chunks.en: he may benefit from Jews without a bris, but not from non-Jews who had a milah.
chunks.st: he is permitted to derive benefit from uncircumcised Jews because they are not regarded as uncircumcised, but he is prohibited from deriving benefit from the circumcised of the nations of the world.

words.note: A Jew who could not have a bris, for health reasons.

chunks.en: "Konam, that I will not benefit from people with a bris milah,"
chunks.st: Conversely, if he said: Benefiting from those who are circumcised is konam for me,

chunks.he: אָסוּר בְּעַרְלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וּמֻתָּר בְּמוּלֵי הַגּוֹיִם,

chunks.st: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:

chunks.en: Rabbi Yishmael says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yishmael says:

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korchah says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Korḥa says:

chunks.st: Great is

chunks.en: Rabbi Nechemyah says,
chunks.st: (see Exodus 4:24–26). Rabbi Neḥemya says:

chunks.en: Milah is great,
chunks.st: So great is

chunks.en: because it pushes aside the laws of tzaraas.
chunks.st: the mitzva of circumcision that it overrides the prohibitions associated with leprosy.
chunks.stMore: If leprosy is found on the foreskin of an infant, although it is generally prohibited to cut the afflicted area, it is permitted to do so to perform the mitzva of circumcision.

words.note: A skin sickness in the Torah.
